chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the divorce that results in her not being permissible for him unless she marries another husband. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'I inform you of what I did with a woman who was with me, and I intended to divorce her. So I left her until when she menstruated and was pure, I divorced her without sexual intercourse, and I bore witness upon that with two witnesses. Then I left her until when she was about to complete her waiting period, I reverted back to her and had sexual intercourse with her, and I left her until when she menstruated and was pure. Then I divorced her upon purity without sexual intercourse with two witnesses. Then I left her until when it was before her waiting period completed, I reverted back to her and had sexual intercourse with her. Until when she menstruated and was pure, I divorced her upon purity without sexual intercourse with witnesses; and I did that with her because there was no need for me with her.'
ai.seo_question: How did the Imam demonstrate the process of triple divorce to make the wife permissible again?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) elucidates the mechanism of *Taliq al-Thalath* by demonstrating a practical precedent where he executed three distinct divorces, each occurring in a state of purity (*tuhr*) without prior sexual intercourse, thereby establishing three separate marital contracts. This narration is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for validating the permissibility of sequential divorces within a single period, countering views that require consummation between each divorce to reset the count. The Imam’s method underscores the legal validity of the husband's intent and the procedural purity of the act, ensuring the wife becomes fully permissible again only after the third marriage is consummated and dissolved.
